claim: A website calling itself the Hanover Institute for Public Policy published 124 reports totaling more than 560,000 words between August 6 and August 14, 2026. An investigation by The Guardian, published August 26, 2026, found no legal entity, no physical address, no named staff and no bylines behind the name; almost every headline is phrased as a question a person would type into a chatbot, and the detection tool GPTZero flagged 11 of 12 sampled reports as machine-written with high confidence. The site's material is registered with the U.S. Justice Department under the Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) — the 1938 law requiring agents of foreign governments to disclose their work — by Piro, Inc., a New York media production company. Piro's own FARA filings name its foreign principal as Havas Media Germany GmbH acting on behalf of the Israel Government Advertising Agency (LaPam), a branch of the Israeli government, and describe the engagement as content work "undertaken on behalf of the Israel Ministry of Foreign Affairs."

notes: The FARA filings are ours, pulled from efile.fara.gov and read with pdftotext; registrant 7732 = Piro, Inc., 244 Fifth Avenue Suite 2144, New York, registered 06/02/2026, foreign principal Havas Media Germany GmbH for LaPam, officials named as Eran Shayovitch and Guy Getz. The report/word counts, the missing-entity finding and the GPTZero result are The Guardian's, carried as attributed reporting, not as our own verification; theguardian.com blocks our fetcher, so the URL is left null and Ynetnews carries the verbatim. What the operation actually did to any chatbot's output is not established by any of these sources and is not claimed here. See also 2025-clock-tower-gpt-framing-001 for the earlier FARA-filed contract language about GPT framing. Guardian byline not captured: the piece is unreachable to our fetcher and the syndicating outlets (Arab News, Ynetnews, Helsinki Times) name the outlet without the byline, so the citation is to the outlet and date only.
